plan_a_advantages: Includes strength and mobility work, crucial for trail running injury prevention and efficiency.
Features a more consistent progression of aerobic volume, building a solid base.
The inclusion of shorter, controlled runs helps to build speed and efficiency.
plan_b_advantages: Offers a slightly longer overall duration of training minutes.
The trail runs in Plan B provide a more realistic representation of the type of running the athlete will be doing.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more balanced approach to building aerobic endurance with a focus on consistent, controlled effort runs, alongside dedicated strength and mobility work. Plan B, conversely, prioritizes recovery to an almost excessive degree, particularly in the initial days, which could hinder the athlete's progress towards speed. While recovery is crucial, Plan A’s structured aerobic sessions and strength work are more directly geared towards improving running performance, especially for a goal of increased speed.
